project_summary: Decomposition of a legacy ERP monolith into domain services

components.name: ERP monolith decomposition
components.description: The current ERP is a single deployable that bundles invoicing, purchasing, stock control, payroll and reporting behind one shared schema. Every module reads and writes the same Oracle tables, so any change to a column requires a coordinated release of the whole application. The first phase maps the real dependencies between modules by tracing SQL access from the application logs of three full business months. Teams agree a bounded context for each domain and write down which tables each context owns and which ones it only reads. Shared tables that several contexts update are split into an owner table and read-only projections kept in sync through change data capture. Invoicing is extracted first because it has the clearest boundary and the highest rate of regulatory change. The invoicing service exposes a REST API and publishes domain events whenever an invoice is issued, corrected or cancelled. A strangler facade routes each request either to the legacy code or to the new service according to a per-tenant feature flag. Purchasing and stock control follow, sharing an event stream so that reservations and goods receipts stay consistent without distributed transactions. Idempotency keys are required on every command to make retries after network failures safe. Payroll stays in the monolith until the end because its calculation rules are legally sensitive and poorly documented. Before touching payroll, the team builds a characterization test suite that records the outputs of the legacy engine for thousands of historical cases. Reporting is rebuilt as a read model fed by the event streams, which removes the heavy analytical queries from the transactional database. The reporting store uses columnar storage and pre-computed aggregates refreshed every few minutes instead of nightly batch jobs. Authentication moves to a central identity provider with single sign-on, replacing three different password schemes found in the code. Authorization is expressed as policies evaluated by each service, with roles synchronized from the identity provider. A shared observability stack collects structured logs, metrics and distributed traces with a correlation identifier on every request. Dashboards and alerts are defined per service with service level objectives agreed with the business owners. The deployment pipeline builds a container image per service, runs unit and contract tests, and promotes the image through staging with automated smoke tests. Database migrations are versioned and applied with a backward compatible expand and contract approach so that rollbacks stay possible. Capacity tests replay production traffic profiles to find the saturation point of each service before the cutover of its tenants. Data migration scripts run in rehearsal mode several times, comparing row counts and checksums between the legacy and the new stores. The cutover of each tenant happens in a low traffic window with a documented rollback plan and a named incident commander. Operations staff are trained on the new runbooks, including how to drain a service, replay a stuck queue and rotate credentials. Security reviews cover threat modelling, dependency scanning, secrets management and penetration tests on the public interfaces. Personal data is classified and encrypted at rest, and access to it is logged in an immutable audit store. Retention rules are applied automatically so that data past its legal retention period is anonymized or deleted. Documentation is generated from the API specifications and the architecture decision records kept in the repository. A governance board reviews every new cross-service dependency to keep the dependency graph acyclic. Cost reports compare the infrastructure bill of the legacy deployment with the new one after each extracted domain. Performance budgets are enforced in the pipeline, failing the build when latency of a critical endpoint regresses by more than ten percent. Knowledge transfer sessions pair legacy maintainers with the new service teams during the first two months of each extraction. The programme closes with a decommissioning plan for the remaining monolith modules, including archived read-only access for auditors. Risks are tracked weekly, the largest being undocumented business rules in payroll and tenants with customizations that bypass the standard flows.

project_summary: Maintenance backlog of small tasks for an online shop
Online shop with search, payments and shipping

components.name: Catalogue search
components.description: The shop needs full text search over the product catalogue. Results must tolerate typos and rank in-stock items higher. Facets for brand, price and size update as the user types. Search analytics record the queries that return nothing.

components.name: Checkout payments
components.description: Checkout accepts cards and local wallets through a hosted payment page. Failed payments are retried with clear messages for the customer. Refunds can be issued partially from the back office. Every payment event is reconciled against the bank statement each night.

components.name: Shipping labels
components.description: Orders are grouped by carrier and printed as labels in batches. Tracking numbers are sent to the customer as soon as the parcel is scanned. Returns generate a prepaid label on request. Carrier rates are cached to keep the checkout fast.
